at censurere.explanation: "At censurere" means "to censor". Do not mix it up with "en censor" (an examiner), who helps grade an exam: "Censoren giver karakteren" (The examiner gives the grade).

sentence.da: Nogle lande vil **censurere** nyhederne, så folk ikke får hele sandheden.
sentence.en: Some countries want to censor the news so people do not get the whole truth.

at checke ind.explanation: "At checke ind" means "to check in". To ask where to check in at the airport, say: "Hvor kan jeg checke ind?" (Where can I check in?).

sentence.da: Vi kan **checke ind** på hotellet klokken to.
sentence.en: We can check in at the hotel at two o'clock.

at checke ud.explanation: "At checke ud" means "to check out", as in leaving a hotel. To ask when you must leave the room, say: "Hvornår skal vi checke ud?" (When do we have to check out?).

sentence.da: Vi skal **checke ud** af hotellet i dag.
sentence.en: We have to check out of the hotel today.

at cirkulere.explanation: "At cirkulere" means "to circulate". To say blood moves around the body, use it for blood: "Blodet cirkulerer rundt i kroppen" (Blood circulates around the body). The start "cirk-" is also in "en cirkel" (a circle).

sentence.da: Rygter kan **cirkulere** hurtigt på en lille arbejdsplads.
sentence.en: Rumors can circulate quickly at a small workplace.

at citere.explanation: "At citere" means "to quote". To say where the words come from, add "fra" (from): "Han citerer fra en tale" (He quotes from a speech).

sentence.da: Man må gerne **citere** en bog, hvis man nævner forfatteren.
sentence.en: You may quote a book if you mention the author.

at cykle.explanation: "At cykle" means "to cycle". It comes from the noun "en cykel" (a bicycle). To say where you cycle to, add "til" (to): "Jeg cykler til skole" (I cycle to school).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **cykle** på arbejde.
sentence.en: I want to cycle to work.

central.explanation: "Central" means "central", as in a place in the middle of a town. When you talk about the most important idea, it means "main": "den centrale idé" (the main idea).

sentence.da: Vi bor i en **central** lejlighed tæt på stationen.
sentence.en: We live in a central apartment close to the station.

champagne.explanation: "Champagne" means "champagne". To suggest celebrating, say: "Skal vi åbne en flaske champagne?" (Shall we open a bottle of champagne?).

sentence.da: Til nytår drikker vi **champagne** og skåler.
sentence.en: At New Year's we drink champagne and toast.

charme.explanation: "Charme" means "charm". When you describe a place, not a person, it works too: "en hytte med charme" (a cottage with charm).

sentence.da: Han har meget **charme**, og alle kan lide ham.
sentence.en: He has a lot of charm, and everyone likes him.

charmerende.explanation: "Charmerende" means "charming". It comes from the verb "at charmere" (to charm). When you describe a place, use it too: "en charmerende by" (a charming town).

sentence.da: Han er **charmerende** og får alle til at smile.
sentence.en: He is charming and makes everyone smile.

chili.explanation: "Chili" means "a chili". To say a dish has chili in it, add "med" (with): "kylling med chili" (chicken with chili).

sentence.da: **Chili** er lille og meget stærk.
sentence.en: Chili is small and very hot.

chips.explanation: "Chips" means "chips or crisps". Do not mix it up with "pommes frites" (French fries), the long fried sticks of potato: "Jeg bestiller pommes frites" (I order French fries).

sentence.da: **Chips** er lavet af kartofler og smager salt.
sentence.en: Chips are made of potatoes and taste salty.

chokerende.explanation: "Chokerende" means "shocking". Do not mix it up with "chokeret" (shocked). To describe what causes the feeling, use "chokerende": "en chokerende nyhed" (a shocking piece of news). To describe how you feel, use "chokeret": "Jeg er chokeret" (I am shocked).

sentence.da: Nyheden var **chokerende**, og alle blev helt stille.
sentence.en: The news was shocking, and everyone went completely quiet.

chokeret.explanation: "Chokeret" means "shocked". To say how you feel, use "chokeret": "Jeg er chokeret" (I am shocked). Do not mix it up with "chokerende" (shocking), which describes what causes the feeling: "Det er chokerende" (That is shocking).

sentence.da: Jeg blev **chokeret**, da jeg hørte nyheden.
sentence.en: I was shocked when I heard the news.

chokolade.explanation: "Chokolade" means "a chocolate". When you order the drink, use "en varm chokolade" (a hot chocolate). The "ch" at the start is spelled like English "ch" but said like "sh".

sentence.da: **Chokolade** er sød og brun.
sentence.en: Chocolate is sweet and brown.

cirka.explanation: "Cirka" means "about". In writing, it is shortened to "ca." before a number: "ca. tre timer" (about three hours).

sentence.da: Det er **cirka** tre kilometer.
sentence.en: It is about three kilometers.

civil.explanation: "Civil" means "a civilian". When you say someone wears no uniform, use "i civil" (in plain clothes): "Politimanden var i civil" (The policeman was in plain clothes). It is also in "civil ulydighed" (civil disobedience).

sentence.da: Soldaten tog uniformen af og gik rundt i **civil**.
sentence.en: The soldier took off the uniform and walked around in plain clothes.

co2.explanation: "CO2" means "carbon dioxide". The word is also the start of "CO2-neutral" (carbon neutral): "Virksomheden vil være CO2-neutral" (The company wants to be carbon neutral).

sentence.da: Når vi kører bil, udleder vi **CO2** til luften.
sentence.en: When we drive a car, we release CO2 into the air.

cornflakes.explanation: "Cornflakes" means "cornflakes". This word has no article, so say "Vi har cornflakes" (We have cornflakes) for the cereal in general. To say you bought one box, use "en pakke cornflakes" (a box of cornflakes).

sentence.da: Jeg spiser **cornflakes** med mælk til morgenmad.
sentence.en: I eat cornflakes with milk for breakfast.

couscous.explanation: "Couscous" means "couscous". It is spelled the same as in English. To say how much you have, name the amount first: "en pose couscous" (a bag of couscous).

sentence.da: Jeg hælder varmt vand over **couscous**.
sentence.en: I pour hot water over couscous.

creme.explanation: "Creme" means "a cream (lotion)". To say what you use for dry skin, say: "Jeg bruger creme mod tør hud" (I use cream for dry skin). Do not mix it up with "fløde" (cream for coffee or cooking): "Jeg vil have fløde i kaffen" (I want cream in my coffee).

sentence.da: Jeg smører **creme** på mine hænder.
sentence.en: I rub cream on my hands.

creme fraiche.explanation: "Creme fraiche" means "crème fraîche". Danish spells it without accents: "creme fraiche", not "crème fraîche".

sentence.da: Jeg putter **creme fraiche** på min bagte kartoffel.
sentence.en: I put crème fraîche on my baked potato.

cykling.explanation: "Cykling" means "cycling". When you talk about cycling as an activity or sport, use "cykling": "Cykling er sundt" (Cycling is healthy). When you say you are riding a bike, use the verb "at cykle" (to cycle): "Jeg cykler" (I am cycling).

sentence.da: Jeg har en cykel og elsker **cykling**.
sentence.en: I have a bicycle and love cycling.

en café.explanation: "En café" means "a café". To suggest meeting at one, use "gå på café" (go to a café): "Skal vi gå på café?" (Shall we go to a café?).

sentence.da: Vi drikker kaffe på en **café**.
sentence.en: We drink coffee at a café.

en campingplads.explanation: "En campingplads" means "a campsite". It is built from "camping" (camping) and "en plads" (a place). When you say there is no room, use "plads" for "room": "Der er ikke plads her" (There is no room here).

sentence.da: På en **campingplads** kan man sove i telt.
sentence.en: On a campsite you can sleep in a tent.

en campus.explanation: "En campus" means "a campus". To say you are at the university grounds, use "på" (on): "Jeg er på campus i dag" (I am on campus today).

sentence.da: Mange studerende bor på eller tæt ved **campus**.
sentence.en: Many students live on or close to campus.

en cardigan.explanation: "En cardigan" means "a cardigan". To say what someone is wearing, use "have ... på" (have on): "Hun har en blå cardigan på" (She is wearing a blue cardigan).

sentence.da: Hun tager en **cardigan** på, når det er køligt.
sentence.en: She puts on a cardigan when it is cool.

en carport.explanation: "En carport" means "a carport". To say the car is parked in it, use "holde" (stand): "Bilen holder i carporten" (The car is parked in the carport). Do not mix it up with "en garage" (a garage with walls): "Bilen står i garagen" (The car is in the garage).

sentence.da: Vi parkerer bilen under vores **carport**.
sentence.en: We park the car under our carport.

en celle.explanation: "En celle" means "a cell", as in biology. It has two more meanings. When you talk about a prison, it means the small room for one prisoner: "Fangen sidder i en celle" (The prisoner sits in a cell). When you talk about a spreadsheet, it means one box: "Skriv tallet i en celle" (Write the number in a cell).

sentence.da: En **celle** er den mindste levende del af en krop.
sentence.en: A cell is the smallest living part of a body.

en censor.explanation: "En censor" means "an external examiner". In Denmark, an outside person sits with the teacher at an oral exam and helps decide the grade. Do not mix it up with "at censurere" (to censor): "De vil censurere nyhederne" (They want to censor the news).

sentence.da: Til den mundtlige prøve sidder der både en lærer og en **censor**.
sentence.en: At the oral test, there is both a teacher and an external examiner.

en cent.explanation: "En cent" means "a cent". Denmark does not use cents. Instead, "en krone" (a krone) is divided into 100 "øre": "Det koster fem kroner og femti øre" (It costs five kroner and fifty øre).

sentence.da: Den koster kun tyve **cent**.
sentence.en: It only costs twenty cents.

en centimeter.explanation: "En centimeter" means "a centimeter". When you give a number, the word does not change: "ti centimeter" (ten centimeters). The start "centi-" means one hundredth, as in "en centiliter" (a centiliter).

sentence.da: Bordet er hundrede **centimeter** langt.
sentence.en: The table is a hundred centimeters long.

en ceremoni.explanation: "En ceremoni" means "a ceremony". To say a ceremony takes place, use "holde" (hold): "De holder en ceremoni for vinderne" (They hold a ceremony for the winners).

sentence.da: Ved en **ceremoni** gør man tingene på en fast, højtidelig måde.
sentence.en: At a ceremony you do things in a fixed, solemn way.

en champignon.explanation: "En champignon" means "a mushroom". Do not mix it up with "en svamp" (a mushroom of any kind, and also a sponge): "Jeg plukker svampe i skoven" (I pick mushrooms in the forest).

sentence.da: Jeg kan godt lide **champignon** på pizza.
sentence.en: I like mushrooms on pizza.

en chance.explanation: "En chance" means "a chance". When you talk about an opportunity, say: "Giv ham en chance" (Give him a chance). When you talk about how likely something is, say: "Der er en chance for regn" (There is a chance of rain).

sentence.da: Hun har en god **chance** for at vinde.
sentence.en: She has a good chance of winning.

en chauffør.explanation: "En chauffør" means "a driver". Use it for a person who drives as a job: "Chaufføren kører bussen" (The driver drives the bus). Do not mix it up with "en bilist" (a person driving their own car): "Mange bilister holder i kø" (Many drivers are standing in a queue).

sentence.da: Bussens **chauffør** hilser på alle.
sentence.en: The bus driver greets everyone.

en cheesecake.explanation: "En cheesecake" means "a cheesecake". To ask for a slice, say: "Jeg vil gerne have et stykke cheesecake" (I would like a piece of cheesecake).

sentence.da: **Cheesecake** laves af flødeost og æg.
sentence.en: Cheesecake is made of cream cheese and eggs.

en chef.explanation: "En chef" means "a boss". The "ch" is said like English "sh". When you talk about the head of a kitchen, use "en køkkenchef" (a head chef): "Køkkenchefen laver menuen" (The head chef makes the menu).

sentence.da: Min **chef** bestemmer på kontoret.
sentence.en: My boss makes the decisions at the office.

en chokoladekage.explanation: "En chokoladekage" means "a chocolate cake". It is built from "chokolade" (chocolate) and "en kage" (a cake). The end "kage" is also in "en gulerodskage" (a carrot cake).

sentence.da: En **chokoladekage** bages med kakao og smør.
sentence.en: A chocolate cake is baked with cocoa and butter.

en cigaret.explanation: "En cigaret" means "a cigarette". To say someone smokes one, use "at ryge" (to smoke): "Han ryger en cigaret" (He smokes a cigarette).

sentence.da: Han tænder en **cigaret** udenfor.
sentence.en: He lights a cigarette outside.

en cirkel.explanation: "En cirkel" means "a circle". To say people sit facing each other in a round shape, use "i en cirkel" (in a circle): "Vi sidder i en cirkel" (We sit in a circle).

sentence.da: En **cirkel** er rund og har ingen hjørner.
sentence.en: A circle is round and has no corners.

en citron.explanation: "En citron" means "a lemon". To say you squeeze one, use "presse" (squeeze): "Jeg presser en citron i vandet" (I squeeze a lemon into the water).

sentence.da: Kan jeg få en skive **citron** i teen?
sentence.en: Can I have a slice of lemon in the tea?

en coach.explanation: "En coach" means "a coach". For a person who trains a sports team, use "en træner" (a coach): "Træneren råber fra sidelinjen" (The coach shouts from the sideline).

sentence.da: Vores **coach** hjælper os med at blive bedre.
sentence.en: Our coach helps us get better.

en computer.explanation: "En computer" means "a computer". To say a laptop, add "bærbar" (portable): "en bærbar computer" (a laptop).

sentence.da: Jeg skriver en e-mail på min **computer**.
sentence.en: I am writing an email on my computer.

en computermus.explanation: "En computermus" means "a computer mouse". It is built from "en computer" (a computer) and "en mus" (a mouse), the same word as for the animal.

sentence.da: Jeg kan ikke klikke, fordi min **computermus** er gået i stykker.
sentence.en: I cannot click because my computer mouse is broken.

en container.explanation: "En container" means "a container", as in a big metal box for waste or goods. For a small container for food, use "en beholder" (a food container): "Jeg putter resterne i en beholder" (I put the leftovers in a container).

sentence.da: De smider gammelt træ i en **container**.
sentence.en: They throw old wood in a container.

en croissant.explanation: "En croissant" means "a croissant". The pastry that English speakers call a Danish pastry is "et wienerbrød" in Denmark: "Jeg tager et wienerbrød til kaffen" (I take a Danish pastry with my coffee).

sentence.da: Til morgenmad spiser jeg en **croissant** med smør.
sentence.en: For breakfast I eat a croissant with butter.

en cykel.explanation: "En cykel" means "a bicycle". It is spelled with y, not i. To say you come by bike, use "på cykel" (by bike): "Jeg kommer på cykel" (I come by bike).

sentence.da: En **cykel** har to hjul.
sentence.en: A bicycle has two wheels.

en cykelhandler.explanation: "En cykelhandler" means "a bike dealer". It is built from "en cykel" (a bike) and "en handler" (a dealer).

sentence.da: Jeg kan købe en ny cykel hos en **cykelhandler**.
sentence.en: I can buy a new bike at a bike dealer.

en cykelhjelm.explanation: "En cykelhjelm" means "a bike helmet". To say you are wearing one, use "have ... på" (have on): "Hun har cykelhjelm på" (She is wearing a bike helmet). To tell someone to put it on, use "tage på" (put on): "Tag din cykelhjelm på" (Put on your bike helmet).

sentence.da: En **cykelhjelm** beskytter dit hoved.
sentence.en: A bike helmet protects your head.

en cykellås.explanation: "En cykellås" means "a bike lock". It is built from "en cykel" (a bike) and "en lås" (a lock). The end "lås" is also in "en dørlås" (a door lock).

sentence.da: Jeg bruger en **cykellås**, så ingen stjæler min cykel.
sentence.en: I use a bike lock so nobody steals my bike.

en cykelparkering.explanation: "En cykelparkering" means "a bike parking area". It is built from "en cykel" (a bike) and "en parkering" (a parking space). To say where you leave your bike, use "parkere" (park): "Du kan parkere din cykel på cykelparkeringen" (You can park your bike at the bike parking area).

sentence.da: Der er en stor **cykelparkering** foran stationen, og den er gratis.
sentence.en: There is a big bike parking area in front of the station, and it is free.

en cykelpumpe.explanation: "En cykelpumpe" means "a bike pump". It is built from "en cykel" (a bike) and "en pumpe" (a pump). The end "pumpe" is also in "en håndpumpe" (a hand pump).

sentence.da: Jeg pumper cyklen op med en **cykelpumpe**.
sentence.en: I pump up the bike with a bike pump.

en cykelsti.explanation: "En cykelsti" means "a bike lane". It is built from "en cykel" (a bike) and "en sti" (a path). Do not mix it up with "et fortov" (a sidewalk), where people walk: "Gå på fortovet" (Walk on the sidewalk).

sentence.da: Der er en ny **cykelsti** langs vejen.
sentence.en: There is a new bike lane along the road.

en cykeltur.explanation: "En cykeltur" means "a bike ride". It is made from cykel (bicycle) and tur (trip). "Tur" also builds other words, such as "en biltur" (a car trip) and "en sejltur" (a boat trip).

sentence.da: Vi tager på **cykeltur** i skoven.
sentence.en: We go on a bike ride in the forest.

en cyklist.explanation: "En cyklist" means "a cyclist". It comes from the verb "at cykle" (to cycle). The ending "-ist" is also in "en turist" (a tourist).

sentence.da: En **cyklist** kører på cykelstien ved siden af vejen.
sentence.en: A cyclist rides on the bike path next to the road.

et center.explanation: "Et center" means "a center". It is the last part of other words, such as "et sundhedscenter" (a health center). Do not mix it up with "et centrum" (the middle of a town): "Jeg bor i centrum" (I live in the town center).

sentence.da: Der er mange butikker i det nye **center**.
sentence.en: There are many stores in the new center.

et centrum.explanation: "Et centrum" means "a center", as in the middle of a town. Do not mix it up with "et center" (a building for an activity, such as shopping): "Vi handler i indkøbscentret" (We shop at the shopping center).

sentence.da: Jeg bor tæt på **centrum** og cykler på arbejde.
sentence.en: I live close to the center and bike to work.

en check-in.explanation: "En check-in" means "a check-in". It comes from the verb "at checke ind" (to check in). To say when it opens, say: "Check-in åbner klokken tolv" (Check-in opens at twelve).

sentence.da: Ved **check-in** får du nøglen til dit værelse.
sentence.en: At check-in, you get the key to your room.

et chok.explanation: "Et chok" means "a shock". To say someone is in shock, use "i chok" (in shock): "Han er stadig i chok" (He is still in shock).

sentence.da: Det var et **chok** at høre om ulykken.
sentence.en: It was a shock to hear about the accident.

et ciffer.explanation: "Et ciffer" means "a digit". Do not mix it up with "et tal" (a number). To say how many digits a number has, say: "Tallet 25 har to cifre" (The number 25 has two digits).

sentence.da: Det sidste **ciffer** i koden er syv.
sentence.en: The last digit in the code is seven.

et cirkus.explanation: "Et cirkus" means "a circus". When you talk about a chaotic situation, it also means "a mess": "Det er et cirkus herhjemme" (It is a circus at home).

sentence.da: Vi skal i **cirkus** i aften og se dyr.
sentence.en: We are going to the circus tonight to see animals.

et citat.explanation: "Et citat" means "a quote". It comes from the verb "at citere" (to quote). To talk about a well-known one, say: "Det er et berømt citat fra Shakespeare" (It is a famous quote from Shakespeare).

sentence.da: Hun bruger et **citat** fra bogen i sin tale.
sentence.en: She uses a quote from the book in her speech.

et computerspil.explanation: "Et computerspil" means "a computer game". It is built from "en computer" (a computer) and "et spil" (a game). To say you play one, use "spille" (play): "Han spiller computerspil" (He plays computer games).

sentence.da: I et **computerspil** styrer man en figur på skærmen.
sentence.en: In a computer game you control a character on the screen.

et cpr-nummer.explanation: "Et CPR-nummer" means "a CPR number". CPR stands for "Det Centrale Personregister" (the Central Person Register). In Denmark, it is the personal ID number that residents are given.

sentence.da: Jeg skriver mit **CPR-nummer** på formularen hos lægen.
sentence.en: I write my CPR number on the form at the doctor's.

et crush.explanation: "Et crush" means "a crush". The word is borrowed from English. To say who the crush is on, use "på" (on): "Jeg har et crush på en kollega" (I have a crush on a coworker).

sentence.da: Hun rødmer, hver gang hendes **crush** smiler til hende.
sentence.en: She blushes every time her crush smiles at her.

et cv.explanation: "Et cv" means "a CV". It is written in lowercase, and the endings come after an apostrophe: "cv'et" (the CV). To say you send one, use "sende" (send): "Jeg sender mit cv til firmaet" (I send my CV to the company).

sentence.da: Jeg skal opdatere mit **cv** i dag.
sentence.en: I have to update my CV today.

et cykelbud.explanation: "Et cykelbud" means "a bike courier". It is built from "en cykel" (a bike) and "et bud" (a messenger).

sentence.da: Et **cykelbud** kom med pizzaen på ti minutter.
sentence.en: A bike courier came with the pizza in ten minutes.

et cykelløb.explanation: "Et cykelløb" means "a bike race". It is built from "en cykel" (a bike) and "et løb" (a race). The end "løb" is also in "et maratonløb" (a marathon).

sentence.da: Til et **cykelløb** vinder den, der først krydser målstregen.
sentence.en: At a bike race, the one who first crosses the finish line wins.

et cykelstativ.explanation: "Et cykelstativ" means "a bike rack". It is built from "en cykel" (a bike) and "et stativ" (a stand).

sentence.da: Jeg låser min cykel fast i et **cykelstativ**.
sentence.en: I lock my bike to a bike rack.
